text:
alina: Heads-up — seeing intermittent PCIe power-rail flicker on gpu-node-104 (eu-west1) starting ~09:42 UTC. Affected card is GPU0. Symptoms: Xid 13 + soft resets, kernel log shows PCIe link up/down, inference tail latency jumps ~3x for pods on that node.

alina: snippet from dmesg:```
[ 4213.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00:00): 13, Ch 00000010, Class 0b00
[ 4213.123789] pcieport 0000:1c:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: id=0005
[ 4213.124001] pcieport 0000:1c:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer
[ 4213.124210] pcieport 0000:1c:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: device [10de:2204] error status/mask=00000000/00002000
```

alina: Also noticed `ipmi sensor` shows transient 12V rail dip to ~11.1V for the chassis power domain during the events. No PSU alarms in OOB yet.

marc: Oof. Are pods on that node stateful? any long-running batches?

jess: There are a couple of Dedicated inference pods pinned to node-104. They have checkpointed state but long requests can be disrupted. We should cordon+drain.

ryan: Is this a single card or multiple? If GPU0 is flaky, we can evict and reprovision. Any ECC errors?

alina: ECC counters bumped on GPU0 — small growth, not explosion. Xid type matches earlier flaky hardware reports. Looks localized to GPU0 and the PCIe root.

marc: Proposed immediate steps: 1) cordon node-104 2) drain pods with --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets 3) power-cycle the node via iDRAC/IPMI 4) reprovision or schedule card swap with on-site tech if power-cycle doesn't clear.

jess: +1. Need to check autoscaler implications: this is in a low-capacity AZ for eu-west, draining could push us into preemption. I'll watch the node groups.

ops-bot: NOTE: maintenance window required for physical swap. If you initiate drain now, autoscaling may spin up new nodes (expected).

marta: Oncall SRE here — approve drain now. Window 20m to keep risk low. Who will own the swap if pwr-cycle fails?

alina: I can own the triage and do a soft power-cycle (ipmitool chassis power cycle) now, then follow up with bench tests. If persists, escalate to on-site tech for card RMA.

ryan: Can you also attach the kernel + NV driver logs to the incident? We'll need timestamps to correlate with Datadog traces.

alina: will upload logs to /mnt/logs/incidents/1976543210/pci-flicker.log and paste link.

alina: link: https://git.internal.redwood/logs/1976543210/pci-flicker.log :eyes:

marc: After drain, set node to maintenance in inventory so autoscaler doesn't immediately reprovision identical hardware into pool. Tag node with `hardware:quarantine`.

jess: I'm watching headroom in eu-west autoscaler — currently 12% spare. If more nodes go we may need emergency burst capacity from dedicated pool.

marta: Approve replacement if power-cycle fails. Please follow RMA playbook: run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `sensors` + `ipmitool sdr` before swapping.

alina: executing steps now: cordon -> drain -> ipmitool cycle. I'll report back in ~10m.

ops-bot: ACTION: cordon(node-104) by alina at 1976543275

alina: cordon done. drain started: `kubectl drain gpu-node-104 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

jess: pods moving off, two long-running inference pods re-created on node-107 and node-112. Observability shows tail-latency returning to baseline for those routes.

alina: power-cycle issued via IPMI. Monitoring for reboots and Xid recurrence.

alina: quick checks post-cycle: `nvidia-smi` shows GPU0 up, ECC counters slightly higher but stable. No immediate Xid. ipmi sensor voltages back to 12.05V.

ryan: Good. Leave node quarantined and run stress test (small synthetic workload) for 30m before returning to pool. Add hardware tag to inventory.

alina: running 30m stress-run `bench-inference --model=q2-small --seq=256 --rps=5 --duration=1800` now. Will share results.

marta: Also open a ticket with colo to inspect PCIe riser and PSU connector when they have a tech on site. I'll create the ticket and link it.

alina: stress-run completed: 30m, no Xid, stable temps, no further PCIe AER in dmesg. Uploading pass logs to the incident folder.

jess: recommend keeping node in quarantine for 24h and monitoring cluster headroom. If no recurrence, we can re-enable and remove `hardware:quarantine` tag.

alina: agree. I'll mark node-104 as `quarantine` and set calendar reminder to review in 24h.

marta: filed colo ticket #COLO-9842 for on-site inspection of riser/PSU connectors. Assign to vendor tech.

ryan: follow-up: add a Datadog alert to catch PCIe AER bursts on any node (threshold: >3 AER events in 5m) so we catch similar before user impact.

marc: thanks team. Good catch and quick response. :thumbsup:
